tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The premise is not established by this test. Its fixture creates symbolic parameters, and test_instance constructs one inverse-curve expression and checks its type/string; the default Float constants belong to the separate test_with_defaults (sympy/physics/biomechanics/tests/test_curve.py:283-320). Function construction is cache-decorated (sympy/core/function.py:444-450), so identical calls need not allocate new expression objects. Repeated tests entail work, but significant suite-wide memory or runtime impact requires profiling; these sources do not show hundreds of repetitions or the claimed Float-allocation bottleneck.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Pow.as_base_exp recognizes a Rational with numerator 1 and denominator other than 1, then returns Integer(denominator), -exponent; otherwise it returns the original base and exponent (sympy/core/power.py:797-823). The identity (1/q)^e=q^(-e) motivates this normal form and consistent downstream decomposition. This is a transformation, not a runtime validation pass. Mathematical equivalence should not be confused with guaranteed structural equality when reconstructing an originally unevaluated power.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: After common Jacobian extraction, _initialize_kindiffeq_matrices stores original coefficients as _f_k_implicit, _k_ku_implicit and _k_kqdot_implicit. It then solves against k_kqdot, builds _qdot_u_map and stores explicit coefficients with an identity qdot matrix (sympy/physics/mechanics/kane.py:364-397). Both sets are initialized: implicit mode does not skip this solve. The explicit_kinematics flag subsequently selects which matrix form the kinematic properties expose.
